extra_audio.text: Thanks for the update, Caio. The deal is gaining traction on our side. Having said that, the optics of the carve-out are a problem for our board. To put it differently, they don't want to buy a company with a hole in the middle. Here's the thing: we don't have the bandwidth to run two integrations. Let me be clear, a separate deal for that unit is a non-starter. Let's table the price for now, and circle back to it on Friday.

Okay, so here's the thing. The deal is gaining traction on our side, and the committee likes your team. Having said that, the optics of the carve-out are kind of a problem. To put it differently, our board doesn't wanna buy a company with a hole in the middle. So we're gonna need a ballpark figure for the whole business by Friday. Let's table the price for now, and circle back to it next week.

For years, I tried to catch every word on calls with American investors, and I always got lost. Then a mentor told me: stop translating, and listen for the signals. When someone says having said that, a problem is coming. When they say to put it differently, you get a second chance. Now, when I miss something, I just say: if I understood correctly, you are saying that. Nobody has ever thought less of me. Most of the time, they explain it again, more slowly.
